claims.text: A market-orientated business is one that finds out what customers want and shapes its products, prices and promotion around that information, rather than making what it finds easiest to produce and then looking for buyers.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Market research information is used to identify customer wants, spot gaps in the market, set prices and promotion that match the target customers, and reduce the risk of decisions by replacing guesses with evidence.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A product-orientated business develops the product first, often from a skill or material it already has, and then searches for customers, whereas a market-orientated business starts from what customers want.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Primary research is first-hand data collected by the business itself, gathered directly from customers or potential customers to answer the business's own specific question.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Secondary research uses data that already exists, collected by someone else for their own purposes, such as government statistics, competitor websites or a commercial market research report.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Primary research tends to give data that is specific, up to date and unavailable to competitors, but it usually costs more and takes longer to gather, and a small or badly chosen sample can mislead.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Secondary research is usually quick and cheap to obtain and often covers a whole industry or country, but it may be out of date, may not fit the business's exact question, and is equally available to competitors.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A postal questionnaire is a printed set of questions mailed to chosen respondents, who return their answers by post; it is cheap per person reached but response rates tend to be low and slow.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: An online survey delivers the same questions over the internet and collects answers as respondents click through; it is fast and close to free to distribute, but it tends to reach the people who are online and willing, so some groups are under-represented.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: An interview is a guided conversation with one respondent, face to face or by phone, allowing follow-up questions and detailed answers; a focus group is a moderated discussion in which six to ten customers react to a product or idea together, revealing reasons behind opinions but risking being swayed by a dominant voice.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A sample is the part of a target market selected to take part in research, whose answers are used to draw conclusions about the whole market.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Surveying every potential customer is usually too costly and slow for a business, so a sample that resembles the market lets it draw conclusions about the whole at a fraction of the cost, provided the sample is chosen with care.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Free online secondary research - competitor websites, social media and trade news - is fast and cheap, but its quality varies from official tables to unsupported claims, so sources are checked before decisions lean on them.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Government sources such as a statistics agency's tables are methodical and usually free or cheap, and they aim at whole populations, but they tend to be broad and may be some years old.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A commercial market research report is written and sold by a specialist agency; it offers depth of industry analysis a small firm could not gather alone, at a price, and competitors are able to buy the same report.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The accuracy of market research data is influenced by the size and representativeness of the sample, the neutrality and clarity of the questions, the honesty and knowledge of respondents, the age of the data, and the care with which results are recorded and analysed.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Inaccurate research data tends to mislead decisions - a launch built on flattering figures can fail in the market - so the cost of checking data before acting on it is usually smaller than the cost of acting on bad data.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Analysing market research data presented in a table or diagram means comparing the figures against each other - which is largest, which rose or fell, by how much - before stating what the pattern means for the business.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A sound conclusion from market research data compares at least two figures, states the size of the pattern, and stays inside what the data can support rather than guessing at causes the figures do not show.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: What separates primary from secondary research is who collected the data and for what question, not its cost, its recency or how closely it fits the business: data gathered first-hand by the business for its own question is primary, while data that already exists, collected by someone else, is secondary even when the business pays for it.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.
